full_judgment:
"Some of the plaintiffs have been paid compensation as per provisional award prepared by the L.A. Collector before the receipt of the cancellation order of the senior Member, Board of Revenue, cancelling the entry in C S. Plot No. 401 in the Collectors Khatian in the record of right. The plaintiffs are not entitled to take advantage of this wrong payment, as the plaintiffs have acquired no right, title or interest over the suit property nor their alleged vendors had any right, title or interest over the suit property." 

 "That the allegations made in paragraphs 10-12 of the petition are not at all true or correct. Some of the plaintiffs have been paid compensation as per provisional Award prepared by the L A. Collector before the receipt of the cancellation order of the Senior Member, Board of Revenue, cancelling the entry in C S Plot No. 401 in the Collector's Khatian in the record of right. The Plaintiffs are not entitled to take advantage of this wrong payment, as the plaintiffs have acquired no right, title or interest over the suit property nor their alleged vendors had any right, title or interest over the suit property. The plaintiffs are nothing but illegal occupants and trespassers after the requisition and acquisition of the kind, The Government can evict the trespassers by the help of Act X of 1953 or by section 12 of the East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act and the plaintiffs cannot resist the Government under the Law." 

 8. Mr. Ranadhir Sen has argued that by the amendment, if allowed, no prejudice will be caused to the plaintiff-opposite parties. Rather the amendment will help determination of the real question in controversy between the parties. The plaintiff opposite parties claim their tenancy right in the suit land on the basis of settlement of their vendors from the Bhowal Estate while the case of the defendant-petitioner is that the land was Khas land of the Bhowal Estate and after the acquisition under the Acquisition and deviancy Act the suit land became the Khas land of the Government as it was not found retainable by the ex-landlord. Mr. Sen further states that at certain stage the land was acquired under the Emergency Requisition Act and some of the plaintiffs got compensation but from this payment of compensation it cannot be said that their ownership was admitted in the land. The compensation might have been paid on the basis of possession. But inadvertently it was stated in para 10 of written statement that provisional compensation was paid to the owners of the land. It seems Mr. Ranadhir Sen has argued rightly that the statement that provisional compensation was paid to the owners of the land was made through inadvertence and that it was nothing but a bonfire mistake which is now sought to be deleted by the proposed amendment. In the khatian also the possession of some of the plaintiffs appears to have been recorded with the remark ‘No title to the land’. In this view of the matter Mr. Ranadhir Sen, we think, has rightly argued that the amendment, if allowed, will not cause any prejudice to any claim of the plaintiff opposite parties.
